overview.headline: Lincoln's 1863 proclamation shifted the Civil War toward freedom

keyPoints.point: President Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863 to free enslaved people in rebellious areas.
keyPoints.quote: President Abraham Lincoln issued the Emancipation Proclamation on January 1, 1863

keyPoints.point: The North initially fought to prevent secession and preserve the Union rather than to end slavery.
keyPoints.quote: was fought by the North to prevent the secession of the Southern states and preserve the Union

keyPoints.point: The preliminary order stated that enslaved people in states still in rebellion on January 1, 1863 would be declared free.
keyPoints.quote: which stated that enslaved people in those states or parts of states still in rebellion as of January 1, 1863, would be declared free

keyPoints.point: The proclamation applied only to seceded states and left slavery untouched in loyal border states.
keyPoints.quote: It applied only to states that had seceded from the Union, leaving slavery untouched in the loyal border states.

keyPoints.point: Federal advances after the proclamation expanded freedom and Black men joined the Union Army and Navy as liberators.
keyPoints.quote: Moreover, the Proclamation announced the acceptance of Black men into the Union Army and Navy, enabling the liberated to become liberators.
